newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet firm on Indonesian factor.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet firm on Indonesian factor.

text.p: The Singapore jet fuel market was firmer on Friday as a trader priced out its cargo sales into Indonesia, while gas oil was steady despite the fall in crude and gas oil futures in London, traders said.
Indonesia has bought 1.3 million barrels of jet fuel and 3.5 million barrels of gas oil for March deliveries.
Traders said a trader bid for jet fuel at $27.50 for March 18-22 lifting fob, 50 cents over Thursday, with no offers seen. Jet was also well bid on the swaps market with few sellers seen.
But traders said refiners should have ample jet fuel supplies for sale and might be waiting for prices to be bid higher.
The firmer jet value was also seen on the wider jet/gas oil spread of $1.40/$1.80, 20-40 cents out from Thursday.
Gas oil was traded again at $25.00 per barrel for March 22-26 lifting fob between two traders, defying some traders expectations that it would soon break $25.00-support.
The steady market also ignored the $2.25 a tonne fall in IPE gas oil futures prices and a 25-cent slide in Brent crude futures as of 1050 GMT.

The swaps gas oil market was volatile as prices slipped below $25.00 a barrel in early trading, rose up to trade at a high of $25.25 and later slipped back to $25.05/$25.10, which was around Thursday's closing level.
Traders said the upswing during the day was due to active buying as some players were pricing out into Indonesia.

But traders said the anticipation of at least three 80,000-tonne cargoes from North West Europe and the Mediterranean--from a Dutch, and two US traders--sometime during end-March and early April was having a bearish effect on later months.
Another dampener was expectations that India would take only three or four cargoes of diesel in its second tender for April delivery, two less than what it tendered for.

The lowest offer for 1.0-percent sulphur diesel was from a European major at $20.48 a tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes c-and-f Kandla. The lowest offer for a 0.5-percent cargo was made by another European major at $28.87 above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f.
